intro: Lesson 16: The Hijrah: the plan, the cave of Thawr and Abu Bakr as-Siddiq. To understand how the Prophet ﷺ planned the Hijrah and trusted Allah in the cave of Thawr

passage.title: Qur'an, at-Tawbah 9:40 (translation of the meaning)
paras: Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us.

questions.q: Explain how the Hijrah shows planning and trust together.
questions.a: They planned camels, a guide, food and a hiding place, then trusted Allah in the cave (9:40).
questions.model: Point: the Prophet ﷺ planned and trusted. Evidence: camels, a guide and the cave were arranged; in the cave he said 'Allah is with us' (9:40). Explain: tawakkul means doing your best and relying on Allah. Link: we plan for exams and still make du'a.

questions.q: How long did they hide in the cave?
Make a Hijrah timeline on the pupil PDF (six events), then write in the portal response box how one event shows tawakkul. Start: 'Tawakkul means ... For example, ...'
questions.a: Six events in order; tawakkul explained with the cave or the plan
questions.model: Teacher places event 1: 'The Quraysh plot to kill the Prophet ﷺ (8:30).'

questions.q: why is Abu Bakr called as-Siddiq?
questions.a: He always believed the Prophet ﷺ and was truthful.

questions.q: why did the Muslims later start their calendar from the Hijrah?
questions.a: It began the first Muslim community and state.

questions.q: Back to our ponder: is trust enough without a plan?
questions.a: No: plan carefully, then trust Allah.
